proof.text: The smooth-projective-curve instance gives SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 f directly from the dimension-one integral curve and smoothness assumptions [def-pc-smooth-projective-curve]. Smooth relative dimension one is stable under base change, as used in IsHilbertSubscheme.isInvertible and abelClass_mem. Smoothness gives flatness and local finite presentation [lem-pc-smooth-flat]; projectivity gives properness [lem-pc-projective-proper], which is preserved by base change [lem-pc-proper-base-change], and hence quasi-compactness and separatedness [def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties].

source.place: Remark 0B9J (remark-universal-object-hilb-d): 'The universal closed object is a relatively effective divisor ... by Lemma 0B9D', whose hypothesis 'X -> S smooth of relative dimension 1' is checked here for X = C_T

proof.text: *Clause 1.* Let $\varphi:h_{H_d}\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Hilb}^d_{C/k}$ be the representing isomorphism [def-pc-representable-functor] and $D_d:=\varphi_{H_d}(\mathrm{id}_{H_d})$. By the definition of the Hilbert functor [def-pc-hilb-functor], $D_d\subset C_{H_d}$ is a closed subscheme with $D_d\to H_d$ finite locally free of degree $d$ [def-pc-finite-locally-free]. By step 1, $C_{H_d}\to H_d$ is smooth of relative dimension $1$, so [lem-pc-cartier-criterion], implication (1)$\Rightarrow$(2), shows that $D_d$ is a relative effective Cartier divisor on $C_{H_d}/H_d$ [def-pc-relative-effective-cartier]: an effective Cartier divisor of $C_{H_d}$, flat over $H_d$. (For $d=0$, $D_d=\emptyset$, whose ideal is $\mathcal O_{C_{H_d}}$; the argument covers it.) Hence its ideal $\mathcal I_{D_d}$ is an effective Cartier ideal and $\mathcal O(D_d)=\mathcal I_{D_d}^\vee$ of [def-pc-divisor-line-bundle] is defined, and it is an invertible $\mathcal O_{C_{H_d}}$-module by [lem-pc-divisor-line-bundle-invertible]. In Lean use D := eH.homEquiv (identity H). Its Hilbert condition gives D.2.isInvertible and D.2.2.1, hence the relative Cartier pair. Use abelClass f D for L, abelClassIso f D for its representative isomorphism, and D.2.isInvertible.isInvertible_dual_toModules for invertibility.

source.place: Remark 0B9J: 'The universal closed object is a relatively effective divisor D_univ ... by Lemma 0B9D ... In particular, D_univ is an effective Cartier divisor and we obtain an invertible module O(D_univ)'; Lemma 0B9D (lemma-divisors-on-curves) (1)=>(2)

proof.text: *The fibre of $\mathcal O(D_d)$ at a point.* Let $t\in H_d$, with residue field $\kappa(t)$ (a field extension of $k$ through $H_d\to\operatorname{Spec}k$, [def-pc-field-extension]) and canonical morphism $\iota_t:\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(t)\to H_d$. The fibre product $C_{H_d}\times_{H_d}\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(t)=(C\times_kH_d)\times_{H_d}\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(t)$ is $C_{\kappa(t)}=C\times_k\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(t)$ (pasting of fibre products, [def-pc-fibre-product]), and the pullback of $\mathcal O(D_d)$ along the projection $\iota_{t,C}:C_{\kappa(t)}\to C_{H_d}$ is the fibre $\mathcal O(D_d)_t$ of [def-pd-fibrewise-degree]. By step 1, $C_{H_d}\to H_d$ is flat of finite presentation, and by step 2 $D_d$ is a relative effective Cartier divisor on it; so [lem-pc-recd-pullback] with $g=\iota_t$ gives: $D_t:=D_d\times_{H_d}\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(t)$ is a relative effective Cartier divisor on $C_{\kappa(t)}/\kappa(t)$, in particular an effective Cartier divisor on $C_{\kappa(t)}$ [def-pc-relative-effective-cartier], and $\mathcal O_{C_{\kappa(t)}}(D_t)\cong\iota_{t,C}^*\mathcal O(D_d)=\mathcal O(D_d)_t$. Moreover $D_t\to\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(t)$ is the fibre of $D_d\to H_d$ over $t$, so, $D_d\to H_d$ being finite locally free of degree $d$, $\dim_{\kappa(t)}\Gamma(D_t,\mathcal O_{D_t})=d$ by [def-pc-finite-locally-free]. These fibre comparisons are already proved in abelClass_mem, using the relative Cartier pullback theorem and the rank-versus-fibre-sections comparison.

source.place: Remark 0B9J, last sentence: 'the restriction of O(D_univ) to the fibre [D] x X is O_X(D)', here at an arbitrary point t of H_d

proof.text: For every point t of H, use abelClass_mem f D and mem_picardSubfunctorDegree_iff to obtain picardPresheafDegree f (abelClass f D) t = d [def-pd-fibrewise-degree, def-pc-degree-line-bundle]. The existing proof of abelClass_mem restricts the dual ideal to the residue-field fibre, uses degree_dual_toModules [lem-pc-degree-base-change], and identifies the dimension of its sections with the Hilbert rank d. This does not require the separate field-extension Krull-dimension theorem.

source.place: Tag 0BA0 proof, first paragraph: Pic^d consists of the L with chi(X_t, L_t) = d + 1 - g, i.e. fibre degree d; the degree of O(D) for D of degree d

proof.text: Let L := abelClass f D and hL := abelClass_mem f D. Let eta be toSheafify for the degree-d Picard subfunctor [def-pc-picard-presheaf, def-pc-picard-functor, def-pd-degree-morphism]. Define gamma := eP.homEquiv.symm (eta.app (op H) (L,hL)). Equiv.apply_symm_apply proves its representing equation [def-pc-representable-functor, lem-pc-yoneda].

source.place: Tag 0BA0 proof, second paragraph: 'There is a morphism gamma_d ... coming from the invertible sheaf O(D_univ) on Hilb^d x_k X (Remark 0B9J) by the Yoneda lemma (Categories, Lemma 001P)'

proof.text: For a field extension K/k and a K-point x of H, put DK := eH.homEquiv x and LK := abelClass f DK. The Hilbert condition gives DK.IsInvertible and invertibility of its dual ideal [def-pc-hilb-functor, def-pc-relative-effective-cartier]. abelClassIso gives the representative isomorphism and abelClass_mem gives degree-d membership. RepresentableBy.homEquiv_comp applied to x and identity H identifies DK with the Hilbert pullback of D [lem-pc-yoneda]. The existing pic_map_abelClass, proved from compatibility of divisor line bundles with pullback [lem-pc-recd-pullback, def-pc-module-pullback], then identifies the Picard restriction of L with LK.

source.place: Remark 0B9J, last sentence (restriction of O(D_univ) to the fibre over the point [D] is O(D)), for a K-point; Proposition 0B9I (2) 'Part (2) follows from the definitions'

proof.text: The equality of Picard classes from step 6 gives an equality in the degree-d subfunctor by Subtype.ext. Apply eP.homEquiv_comp to x and gamma, replace eP.homEquiv gamma by the defining sheafification image, and use naturality_apply of toSheafify [def-pc-picard-presheaf, def-pc-module-pullback, def-pc-picard-functor]. This proves the required equation for x composed with gamma.

split_report.summary: Split following Stacks 0BA0 (4) and the second paragraph of its proof (gamma_d from O(D_univ) by Yoneda), Remark 0B9J and Lemma 0B9D. Seven steps: (1) C_T -> T smooth of relative dimension 1, flat, proper, of finite presentation (new unsplit node for the relative-dimension claim, which the imported Hilbert nodes took as 'standard'); (2) clause 1 from 0B9D (1)=>(2) and the invertibility of O(D); (3) the fibre of O(D_d) at t is O(D_t) by the base-change lemma lem-pc-recd-pullback, D_t of length d by the definition of degree d; (4) clause 2 from deg O(D) = dim Gamma(O_D) (lem-pc-degree-base-change (2)) on the 1-dimensional proper C_{kappa(t)}; (5) gamma_d defined from the class via the representing isomorphism of Pic^d; (6)-(7) clause 3 by Yoneda for the Hilbert functor (x corresponds to D_d x_{H_d} Spec K) and naturality of the Pic^d isomorphism. Statement unchanged; stmt_deps gained def-pc-relative-effective-cartier, def-pc-finite-locally-free, def-pc-base-change, def-sc-effective-cartier-divisor, which the statement uses. lem-pc-universal-divisor (Lean-closed) was not cited: its node statement covers only degree d+1 >= 1, the scheme underline Hilb, and k-rational points, while the item needs every d >= 0, any representing H_d, and K-points; its Lean declaration isRelativeEffectiveCartier_universal_hilbertPresheaf does cover clauses 1 and the pullback part of step 6 in full generality. No slopmaster2 declaration constructs gamma_d.

lean.statement: theorem exists_hilbertToPicardMorphism {k : Type u} [Field k] [IsSepClosed k] {C : Scheme.{u}} (f : C ⟶ Spec (.of k)) [IsSmoothProjectiveCurve f] [GeometricallyIntegral f] (d : ℕ) (H P : Over (Spec (.of k))) (eH : (hilbertPresheaf f d).RepresentableBy H) (eP : (picardFunctorDegree f d).obj.RepresentableBy P) : let D := (eH.homEquiv (𝟙 H)).1 D.IsRelativeEffectiveCartier (pullback.snd f H.hom) ∧ D.toModulesᵛ.IsInvertible ∧ ∃ L : (pullback f H.hom).Pic, Nonempty ((fromSkeleton _).obj L.val ≅ D.toModulesᵛ) ∧ (∀ t : H.left, picardPresheafDegree f L t = (d : ℤ)) ∧ ∃ (hL : L ∈ (picardSubfunctorDegree f d).obj (op H)) (γ : H ⟶ P), eP.homEquiv γ = (toSheafify (Scheme.fppfTopology.over (Spec (.of k))) (picardSubfunctorDegree f d).toFunctor).app (op H) ⟨L, hL⟩ ∧ ∀ (K : Type u) [Field K] [Algebra k K] (x : Over.mk (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k K))) ⟶ H), let T := Over.mk (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k K))) let DK := (eH.homEquiv x).1 DK.IsInvertible ∧ DK.toModulesᵛ.IsInvertible ∧ ∃ (LK : (pullback f T.hom).Pic) (hLK : LK ∈ (picardSubfunctorDegree f d).obj (op T)), Nonempty ((fromSkeleton _).obj LK.val ≅ DK.toModulesᵛ) ∧ eP.homEquiv (x ≫ γ) = (toSheafify (Scheme.fppfTopology.over (Spec (.of k))) (picardSubfunctorDegree f d).toFunctor).app (op T) ⟨LK, hLK⟩

reviewed_lean.note: k sep. closed [IsSepClosed]; C smooth projective [f.IsSmoothProjectiveCurve] + [GeometricallyIntegral f]; d : ℕ; H_d via (hilbertPresheaf f d).RepresentableBy H, D = eH.homEquiv (𝟙 H); P_d via (picardFunctorDegree f d).obj.RepresentableBy P (FIX: replaced the delivered private degree subfunctor Q/hQ of picardFunctor, H4/H12); (1) IsRelativeEffectiveCartier + O(D) invertible; (2) L ≅ O(D), fibre degree d, L ∈ picardSubfunctorDegree f d, eP.homEquiv γ = toSheafify class of ⟨L,hL⟩; (3) all K/k in Type u, x : Spec K ⟶ H, DK effective Cartier, eP.homEquiv (x ≫ γ) = class of O(DK) in Pic^d; g unused; no hollow hypotheses
